critical_code_review_comments: server.py now 10,246 lines — module split still pending (noted in prior iterations).

LIVE module purchase endpoint does not use a DB transaction; a failure mid-loop (e.g. during insert of the 2nd of 3 customers) would leave the first customer's purchase + wallet decrement committed while the batch is partially done. Consider wrapping the per-customer block in a transaction or at minimum returning HTTP 207 Multi-Status with explicit `failed[]` tracking (currently it does track failed but with 200 OK, which may silently mislead the UI).

`create_live_module_purchases` increments `total_sales` by (price+tax) only. Verify this matches how Live Shopping's regular purchase endpoint aggregates `total_sales` (it also uses price_with_tax, so OK — but tested only indirectly).
Product history uses a case-insensitive substring filter in Python after fetching 200 rows — fine for current scale but a Mongo-side `$regex` with index on `name_lower` would scale better.
seed_data_creation: Created several TEST_live_module_* and TEST_dbg lives + a few test purchases (FE_PROD_X, TEST_PROD_*, TEST_NOCOMM_*) on the demo tenant's 'Live Fast Test' live and newly created test lives. D1001 wallet decremented ~$44 during testing. No data created on the main tenant. If cleanup is needed the test lives are easy to spot (TEST_* prefix).
context_for_next_testing_agent: All feature acceptance criteria from the review request are verified. Backend tests are repeatable (test_live_module.py creates its own live each run via module-scoped fixture). The one caveat: tests create seed data each run on the demo tenant and don't clean it up — if accumulation becomes an issue, add a teardown that deletes lives/purchases with the TEST_ prefix.
